title: Loading up on site-specific theatre recently, but I think this is my ...
transcript: if you ever wanted to see theatre performed in an actual restaurant after hours well now's your chance the audience sits at tables to watch this play and your ticket includes a free mug of tomato soup plus you can order other food and drinks before the show but there also is a lot more to this play besides the immersive, site-specific setting. inspired by a New York Times article from 2017, “oh, Honey!” is about a group of women whose sons have all been accused of SA and they formed this support group that meets once a month at this diner that description might make the play sound super heavy and obviously it does deal with some serious topics but there's also an off beat quirkiness throughout the play that's kind of tied together with a heightened sense of reality and they approach this subject matter in ways that make this play a little bit of a tough nut to crack it's not always immediately obvious how all of the narrative and stylistic tangents in the play fit together but to me they all seem to align with each other in spirit I think the play is less interested in conveying a concrete message and more interested in painting this kind of chaotic almost fugue-like character study of these women and how they're socialised to interact with each other to the people around them especially their server at this restaurant and ultimately their sense of duty to their sons I don't think the play necessarily needed to be performed in a real life restaurant but I think the hyper-intimate, site-specific setting really forces you to sit with these characters both physically and psychologically in all of their flaws and humanity people that we empathize with even though we're uncomfortable sometimes with what they're fighting for and fighting through so if you're interested in checking this out “oh, Honey!” is being presented by Ugly Face Theatre and it's performed at the Little Egg restaurant in Prospect Heights, Brooklyn through November 7th
